collections.description: Historical cuts from A specimen of printing types and ornaments from the Baltimore Type Foundry (1832).
collections.observed: 381 historical design identities from the unpaginated1832 Baltimore specimen. Two eagle drawings use clearer repeat impressions in GPO1904, printed169/PDF185/archive185; both original Baltimore witnesses remain retained. Source records distinguish each book and locator.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Thresholding, documented crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the scanned impressions. Names, search tags, Private Use assignments, scale and bearings are new project work. Paper, catalogue numbers and prices are excluded. Multi-tone companions separate observed ink strengths into three disjoint vector regions at default opacities 1, 0.55 and 0.25; these are modern interpretations, not evidence of separately printed inks. Format-specific downloadable-font approximations include modern fine diagonal coverage screening for seven especially dense cuts; original engraved linework remains in the master and SVG. In version 1.001, 167 complete cuts and their tone layers receive documented rigid rotations to level observed frames or bases; no historical contour is redrawn or removed. Version 1.002 restores the full observed upper boundaries of Primer panels 357-01–357-24 from PDF page 209, including previously clipped illustration detail; original scale, position, advances and reviewed rotations are retained.

collections.font_delivery_note: All downloadable fonts use reviewed simplifications for the most detailed engravings. The editable master, SVGs and tonal PNGs retain the full historical outlines; use SVG for enlarged artwork.

collections.name: Baltimore Initials 1832
collections.designer: Baltimore Type Foundry; individual engravers generally unidentified (signed large cuts credited in the source inventory)
collections.foundry: Baltimore Type Foundry; F. Lucas, Jr., agent
collections.description: Historical decorated letters, figures and punctuation from Baltimore 1832 and matching period sources in Boston 1832, Howe 1830 and Bruce 1828, plus the leafy-descender Oak Leaf R.
collections.observed: 80 complete ornamental sorts: 38 original Baltimore impressions, 27 matching period impressions, the complete-sheet Oak Leaf R, and 14 Bruce 1828 additions. Bruce supplies lottery figures 3, 4, 5 and comma, and the complete ornamented SODA water. setting. Its S, a and e have distinct hatched/internal decoration from the related Baltimore and Boston versions. Every item retains an exact crop and citation.
collections.reconstructed: No inferred letters or new pictorial content. Thresholding, crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the observed impressions. Source identifiers, Private Use assignments, uniform scale and bearings are digital metadata and metrics. Original 38 items retain their existing monochrome and three-tone drawings, including reviewed 1.001 alignment. The 42 supplementary impressions are monochrome. No incomplete alphabet is offered as a text font.

collections.foundry: Baltimore Type Foundry; F. Lucas, Jr., agent
collections.description: Historical ornaments from A specimen of printing types and ornaments from the Baltimore Type Foundry (1832).
collections.observed: Impressions from the 1832 Baltimore specimen. Every crop is mapped to a one-based PDF page of this unpaginated book; original JP2 leaves and exact preparation records are retained.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Thresholding, documented crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the scanned impressions. Names, search tags, Private Use assignments, scale and bearings are new project work. Paper, catalogue numbers and prices are excluded. Multi-tone companions separate observed ink strengths into three disjoint vector regions at default opacities 1, 0.55 and 0.25; these are modern interpretations, not evidence of separately printed inks. Separations between joined repeat pieces are inferred from their printed arrangement; complete strips retain the observed context. Version 1.001 applies reviewed rigid rotations to 230 icons to level measured horizontal references, preserving every contour, original scale and advance; source/straightening.json records the evidence and matrices.

collections.foundry: Boston Type & Stereotype Foundry; John G. Rogers, agent
collections.description: Pictorial cuts and ornaments from the Boston Type & Stereotype Foundry specimen of 1832, with shared designs cross-referenced to the existing collection.
collections.observed: Observed impressions from the 1832 Boston specimen. The numbered cut sequence, separate set members, unnumbered impressions and existing-collection equivalents are recorded in source/inventory.json.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Thresholding, documented crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the scanned impressions. Names, search tags, Private Use assignments, scale and bearings are new project work. Paper, catalogue numbers and prices are excluded. Multi-tone companions separate observed ink strengths into three disjoint vector regions at default opacities 1, 0.55 and 0.25; these are modern interpretations, not evidence of separately printed inks. Downloadable fonts use documented bounded approximations for 79 oversized engravings. Ten especially dense cuts use modern diagonal coverage screening to preserve shading; the full historical engraved contours remain in the canonical artwork and SVGs.

revival.notes: Native JP2 sources, exact crop recipes, source-number inventory and shared-design references accompany the canonical artwork. No missing pictorial content is invented. No.470 uses the clearer matching Bruce1828 PDF243 No.288 impression; the original Boston witness remains retained. Stable ID, codepoint and advance are unchanged.

collections.font_delivery_note: All downloadable fonts use reviewed simplifications for the most detailed engravings. The editable master, SVGs and tonal PNGs retain the full historical outlines; use SVG for enlarged artwork.

collections.foundry: Boston Type Foundry; holiday cuts cast by Central Type Foundry
collections.description: Historical ornaments, pictorial cuts, decorated initials and symbols from the Boston Type Foundry specimen of 1889.
collections.observed: Individually catalogued historical impressions from the 1889 Boston specimen; see each icon and source/inventory.json for subjects, pages, specimen numbers, crop evidence and review status.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Thresholding, documented crop cleanup, cubic curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the scanned impressions. Names, search tags, Private Use assignments, scale and bearings are new project work. Paper, catalogue numbers and prices are excluded. Multi-tone companions separate observed ink strengths into three disjoint vector regions at default opacities 1, 0.55 and 0.25; these are modern interpretations, not evidence of separately printed inks.

revival.notes: Canonical monochrome master. Source numbers identify impressions; size alone does not define another digital design. See source/inventory.json and source/METHOD.md. Matching Bruce1828 impressions improve selected drawings; prior source witnesses, stable identities and advances are retained.

collections.name: Bruce Ornaments 1828
collections.designer: Individual engravers unidentified in the specimen
collections.description: Geometric and floral dashes, masks, border repeats, corners and rosettes from George Bruce’s 1828 specimen.
collections.observed: One hundred and ninety-eight distinct drawings: 45 ornamental dashes and masks from unnumbered PDF pages 169–175, and 153 border repeats, corners and floral motifs from pages 177–235. Inventories link repeated settings to the selected Bruce, Baltimore and Boston designs.
collections.reconstructed: No invented pictorial content. Recorded crops exclude isolated scan specks and neighbouring artwork. Cubic fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the native pixels. Measured rigid rotations straighten the dashes; quadrilateral rectification follows tilted border-block edges while retaining the mean opposing edge lengths. Search labels, tags, Private Use assignments and digital metrics are new project work. Small grayscale crops on PDF235 use fourfold working interpolation for stable curve fitting, without adding source detail. Fine hatching unresolved in the source is not reconstructed.

collections.name: GPO Cuts 1897
collections.designer: Historical engravers unidentified except for signatures retained in the impressions
collections.foundry: U.S. Government Printing Office; original cut suppliers not specified
collections.description: Distinct historical seals and emblems from the Government Printing Office specimen of 1897.
collections.observed: Fourteen complete compositions from the 1897 seal pages. The inventory also records twenty-two witnesses of existing GPO designs and one repeated Agriculture seal.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Native crops, measured caption and paper-speck removal, curve fitting and uniform scaling interpret the historical impressions. Three tonal regions interpret scanned ink strength. Names, tags, Private Use assignments, bearings and a blank space are new project work.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann

collections.name: GPO Cuts 1904
collections.designer: Historical engravers unidentified except for signatures retained in the impressions
collections.foundry: U.S. Government Printing Office, Job Room; original cut suppliers not specified
collections.description: Historical pictorial cuts, seals, ornamental wordmarks, borders, binding ornaments, brass rules and technical signs from Government Printing Office specimens of 1897, 1900 and 1904.
collections.observed: Complete historical compositions and measured border components, with repeated and existing-design witnesses recorded individually. Exact native source pages, measured crops and source identification evidence are retained.
collections.reconstructed: No new pictorial content. Crop selection, noise removal, quarter-turn orientation, curve fitting and font-unit rounding interpret the historical impressions. Three tonal regions interpret scanned ink strength, not separate historical inks. Names, tags, Private Use assignments, bearings and a blank space are new project work.

revival.author: Harold Lehmann
revival.notes: Source inventories retain every reviewed impression, repeat, related composition and source-quality decision. Names describe the artwork; the phoenix is classified by its burning pyre despite its placement under Eagle Cuts. Matching Bruce1828 impressions improve selected drawings; prior source witnesses, stable identities and advances are retained.
